children: Malaysia's exports in August likely rose 38.4% on year, similar to July's 38% increase, according to the median estimate of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Imports likely increased 34.9%, leading to a trade surplus of 24.0 billion ringgit. Export growth remained robust, supported by favorable base effects, DBS economists Taimur Baig and Chang Wei Liang say in a note. Export momentum was likely anchored by the electrical and electronics segment amid strong AI-related demand, while oil and gas exports grew at a more moderate pace than their April peak, reflecting weaker energy prices, they add. The trade data are due Friday. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
